A cache hit is only reused if `not self.auto_reload or template.is_up_to_date` (the loader's `uptodate` callable); with `auto_reload=False` stale templates are served forever. `create_cache` maps cache_size==0 to None (no caching, recompile on every request), cache_size<0 to a plain unbounded dict, otherwise an `LRUCache(size)` (default 400). Volatility only arises from `{% autoescape %}`/EvalContextModifier with a non-constant value (`visit_EvalContextModifier` sets `frame.eval_ctx.volatile = True` on Impossible). Since the EvalContext is built from `environment.autoescape` plus the template *name* at compile time, a callable autoescape is evaluated once per template name; `select_autoescape` has `default_for_string=True`, so templates compiled with no name (e.g. `from_string`) are autoescaped, while unknown extensions fall back to `default` (False).","lines":["src/jinja2/compiler.py:1470-1496","src/jinja2/compiler.py:1969-1992","src/jinja2/nodes.py:76-84","src/jinja2/utils.py:581-630"],"check":"import os, sys try: import jinja2 except ImportError: sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'src')); import jinja2 from jinja2 import Environment, select_autoescape env = Environment(autoescape=select_autoescape()) assert env.from_string('{{ x }}').render(x='') == '<b>' plain = Environment() assert 'str(' in plain.compile('{{ x }}', raw=True) esc = Environment(autoescape=True) assert 'escape(' in esc.compile('{{ x }}', raw=True) "},{"id":"g3","kind":"general","question":"When does using an unknown filter or test fail at compile time and when only at render time, and what exception is raised in each case?","key":"`_filter_test_common` in the compiler calls `self.fail(f"No {type_name} named {name!r}.", node.lineno)` -> `TemplateAssertionError` at compile time, but only `if func is None and not frame.soft_frame`. Frames inside `{% if %}`/`{% elif %}` bodies and conditional expressions are soft frames (`Frame.soft()`), so there the check is skipped. When `environment.sandboxed` is true the compiler emits `environment.call(context, ...)` instead of `context.call(...)` for calls, and `environment.call_binop/call_unop(context, op, ...)` for operators listed in `environment.intercepted_binops`/`intercepted_unops`; `nodes.BinExpr/UnaryExpr.as_const` also refuse to constant-fold intercepted operators. The actual safety (`getattr`/`getitem` checks, `is_safe_attribute`, `call`) lives in `jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment`; flipping the flag on a plain Environment generates calls to methods that don't implement any restrictions (and `intercepted_binops` doesn't even exist), so it provides no security. Note also that `SandboxedEnvironment` intercepts no operators by default — you must subclass and set `intercepted_binops`.","lines":["src/jinja2/environment.py:267-271","src/jinja2/compiler.py:61-98","src/jinja2/compiler.py:1875-1896","src/jinja2/nodes.py:499-536"],"check":"import os, sys try: import jinja2 except ImportError: sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'src')); import jinja2 from jinja2 import Environment from jinja2.sandbox import SandboxedEnvironment assert Environment.sandboxed is False assert 'context.call(' in Environment().compile('{{ f() }}', raw=True) assert 'environment.call(context, ' in SandboxedEnvironment().compile('{{ f() }}', raw=True) assert 'environment.call_binop' not in SandboxedEnvironment().compile('{{ a + b }}', raw=True) class S(SandboxedEnvironment): intercepted_binops = frozenset(['+']) assert 'environment.call_binop' in S().compile('{{ a + b }}', raw=True) "},{"id":"g5","kind":"general","question":"How do the filesystem-backed loaders stop a template name from escaping the configured search directory, and what name forms are rejected?","key":"Every path-based loader runs the name through `split_template_path`, which splits on '/' and raises `TemplateNotFound` if any piece equals `os.path.pardir` ('..') or contains `os.sep` (or `os.path.altsep`, e.g. '\\' on Windows); empty pieces and '.' are dropped. The surviving pieces are joined with `posixpath.join` onto the search path (even on Windows, to avoid 'drive:' or UNC segments breaking out), and `os.path.normpath` is applied to the result. So 'a/../b' or 'a\\b' (on Windows) raise TemplateNotFound rather than reaching outside the root; note the check is purely lexical — symlinks inside the search path are still followed.","lines":["src/jinja2/loaders.py:25-39","src/jinja2/loaders.py:194-226","src/jinja2/loaders.py:365-401"],"check":"import os, sys try: import jinja2 except ImportError: sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'src')); import jinja2 from jinja2.loaders import split_template_path from jinja2 import TemplateNotFound assert split_template_path('a/./b.html') == ['a', 'b.html'] assert split_template_path('/a//b') == ['a', 'b'] for bad in ('../x', 'a/../b', 'a/..'): try: split_template_path(bad); raise AssertionError('expected TemplateNotFound for ' + bad) except TemplateNotFound: pass "},{"id":"g6","kind":"general","question":"What sharing happens between environments created implicitly by `Template(...)` and between an environment and its `overlay()`, and which of that sharing is a hazard?","key":"`Template.__new__` routes through `get_spontaneous_environment`, an `lru_cache(maxsize=10)` keyed by the environment class and all the constructor arguments, and marks the result `shared = True`. So all templates built directly with the same options share one Environment object; mutating it (adding filters/globals) affects every such template, and only ten distinct configurations are kept alive by the cache. `overlay()` does `rv.__dict__.update(self.__dict__)`, so mutable state such as `globals`, `filters`, `tests` and `policies` are the *same objects* as the parent's — only the overridden attributes, the cache (`create_cache`/`copy_cache`, always emptied) and the extensions (re-bound via `Extension.bind`, cannot be removed) are fresh. The docstring also warns that modifying an environment after templates are loaded leads to undefined behavior.","lines":["src/jinja2/environment.py:68-80","src/jinja2/environment.py:387-456","src/jinja2/environment.py:1164-1211"],"check":"import os, sys try: import jinja2 except ImportError: sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'src')); import jinja2 from jinja2 import Environment, Template t1 = Template('{{ x }}'); t2 = Template('{{ y }}') assert t1.environment is t2.environment and t1.environment.shared is True e = Environment(cache_size=10) o = e.overlay(autoescape=True) assert o.overlayed is True and o.linked_to is e assert o.globals is e.globals and o.filters is e.filters assert o.cache is not e.cache and len(o.cache) == 0 assert o.autoescape is True and e.autoescape is False "},{"id":"g7","kind":"general","question":"What rules does the engine enforce around `{% block %}` names, duplicate blocks and the `required` modifier, and at which stage is each enforced?","key":"Duplicate block names are a compile-time error: `visit_Template` collects `node.find_all(nodes.Block)` and calls `self.fail(f"block {name!r} defined twice", lineno)` -> `TemplateAssertionError`. Block names must be valid Python identifiers; the parser raises a dedicated TemplateSyntaxError for hyphens. A `required` block's body is checked at parse time to contain only whitespace/comment output ('Required blocks can only contain comments or whitespace'). The 'required' semantics itself is runtime: `visit_Block` emits `if len(context.blocks['name']) <= 1: raise TemplateRuntimeError("Required block 'name' not found")`, so it only fails when the template defining it is rendered without a child overriding the block.","lines":["src/jinja2/compiler.py:845-851","src/jinja2/compiler.py:945-992","src/jinja2/parser.py:292-322"],"check":"import os, sys try: import jinja2 except ImportError: sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'src')); import jinja2 from jinja2 import Environment, DictLoader from jinja2.exceptions import TemplateAssertionError, TemplateRuntimeError, TemplateSyntaxError env = Environment() try: env.from_string('{% block a %}{% endblock %}{% block a %}{% endblock %}'); raise AssertionError('dup') except TemplateAssertionError: pass try: env.from_string('{% block a required %}x{% endblock %}'); raise AssertionError('required body') except TemplateSyntaxError: pass e2 = Environment(loader=DictLoader({'p': '{% block b required %}{% endblock %}', 'c': '{% extends "p" %}{% block b %}hi{% endblock %}'})) assert e2.get_template('c').render() == 'hi' try: e2.get_template('p').render(); raise AssertionError('expected TemplateRuntimeError') except TemplateRuntimeError: pass "}]}
